chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad and Abdullah ibn Sinan, altogether, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is befitting for the guardians of the deceased among you that they should announce to the brethren of the deceased his death, so that they may witness his funeral, pray over him, and seek forgiveness for him; thus, reward is recorded for them, and forgiveness is recorded for the deceased; and he (the announcer) earns reward for them and for what they earned for their deceased through seeking forgiveness.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَيِّتِ: Guardians or close relatives of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the proper procedure for announcing death and seeking forgiveness for the deceased in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the communal obligation of announcing death to facilitate collective supplication, emphasizing the interconnectedness of the living and the dead in the spiritual economy. It highlights that the reward for the deceased is not static but can be actively increased through the specific acts of attendance, funeral prayer, and intercessory forgiveness performed by their community.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Wallad and Abdullah bin Sinan, altogether, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It is befitting for the guardians of the deceased among you that they should be proclaiming to the brethren of the deceased of his death, so that they would be witnessed his funeral, and they would be praying Salaat over him, and they would be seeking Forgiveness for him, so the Recompense would be written for them and the Forgiveness would be written for the deceased; and he (the proclaimer of the news of death) would be earning he Recompensed regarding them and regarding what their deceased would be earning from the Forgiveness’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father all from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad and ’Abd Allah ibn Sinan all who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The guardians of a deceased should inform the brothers (in belief) of the deceased about his death so they may attend his funeral services, perform prayer and appeal on his behalf for forgiveness (from Allah). Thus, a reward for them is written down as well as forgiveness. Also the person informing others about the funeral services earns a reward in addition to forgiveness for the deceased person.”’
